title: Pakistan Extends Airspace Ban on Indian Aircraft Through September 24
detail: The Pakistan Airports Authority issued a fresh NOTAM on August 19, 2026 extending its closure of Pakistani airspace to all India-registered aircraft — including commercial and military flights — through the Lahore and Karachi Flight Information Regions until 4:59am PST on September 24. It is the 16th consecutive extension of the ban Pakistan imposed on April 23, 2025 in response to India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty after the Pahalgam attack, with tensions compounding after India's May 6-7, 2025 strikes on Pakistani cities. India maintains a reciprocal ban on Pakistani aircraft in its own airspace.

media.caption: Pakistan Airports Authority extends the airspace closure to Indian aircraft for a 16th consecutive time, through September 24, 2026

title: US Ambassador Sergio Gor Calls J&K 'Important Part of India' in Srinagar; Pakistan Summons US Chargé d'Affaires
detail: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, on his first visit to Jammu & Kashmir, told a joint media briefing with J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar on August 19, 2026 that Kashmir 'is an important part of India and an incredibly beautiful place,' praising the Centre and state government's security improvements and signaling the US would reconsider its travel advisory for the region. Gor, who also serves as President Trump's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, drew an immediate protest from Islamabad: Pakistan's Foreign Office summoned US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker and lodged a 'strong demarche,' calling the remarks 'factually incorrect' and a departure from the US's longstanding position that J&K is a disputed territory whose final status must be resolved per UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.
